Issues.Title: fix(core): correctly inherit component metadata in JIT undecorated base classes
Issues.Body:
When a bare class extends a component, the JIT compiler compiles it as an abstract directive. Previously, this caused the compiler to skip inheriting the component's metadata into the bare class due to an incorrect throw, or the bare class was skipped completely because `getDirectiveDef` looked up the prototype chain.

This PR updates the `addDirectiveDefToUndecoratedParents` helper to use `Object.hasOwn` to ensure bare classes receive their own `ɵdir` containing their inputs/outputs, and updates `ɵɵInheritDefinitionFeature` to permit these abstract directives to inherit from components.

Issues.Title: fix(docs-infra): link directive selector aliases to the right API page
Issues.Body:
`extractAliasesFromSelector` collects every `[attr]` in a selector, including ones inside `:not(...)` and compound selectors, so `NgModel` and `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` both claim `ngModel`, `formControl` and `formControlName`. `mapManifestToEntries` writes aliases with no collision check, so the last claimant wins (`SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor`), and an alias can also delete a real entry, which is why `email()` never linked.

Aliases are now collected per name. When several directives claim one, the one named after it wins, otherwise it stays unlinked. An alias never replaces a real entry, and `email` joins the names that are not linked on their own (`required`, `min`, ...).

| Text | Links to today | Links to now | Links | Pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ngModel` | `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` | `NgModel` | 56 | 13 |
| `formControlName` | `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` | `FormControlName` | 23 | 6 |
| `formControl` | `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` | `FormControlDirective` | 11 | 3 |
| `routerLink` | `RouterLinkWithHref` | `RouterLink` | 63 | 12 |
| `formGroup`, `formArray` | `NgForm` | `FormGroupDirective`, `FormArrayDirective` | 13 | 5 |
| `formGroupName`, `formArrayName` | `NgControlStatusGroup` | `FormGroupName`, `FormArrayName` | 5 | 1 |
| `ngFor` | `NgForOf` | `NgFor` | 6 | 4 |
| `email()`, `required()`, ... | not linked | `forms/signals/*` | 61 | 12 |

https://angular.dev/guide/forms/form-validation#:~:text=actor%2Dform%2Dtemplate.component.html%20(name)
Hovering `[(ngModel)]` in the form-validation guide, before (angular.dev) and after (this branch):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18cae50f-3215-4812-8d1c-263254002cf7

Diffed every link in the generated guide HTML before and after: 178 wrong links removed, 238 added. Four aliases now render unlinked (`type`, `multiple`, `ngNoCva`, `ngNoForm`).

Issues.Title: docs: add DevTools signal graph guide
Issues.Body:
Fixes angular/angular#71238.

The DevTools section on angular.dev has guides for Components, Profiler, Injectors, and the Router Tree, but none for the signal graph — the navigation config even carried a commented-out placeholder for it. This PR:

- adds `tools/devtools/signals.md`, a new guide that explains how to open the signal graph (the **Show Signal Graph** button in the component property pane, or **Show in signal graph** from a signal property's context menu), how to read the graph (node kinds: signal, computed, effect, linked signal, template, resource clusters; edges showing upstream dependencies / downstream dependents), how to search nodes by name, and how to use the details panel (view source, set breakpoint, watch signal, highlight dependency paths);
- enables the navigation entry (`tools/devtools/signals`) that was commented out as a TODO;
- adds a short "Debugging signals" cross-link in `guide/signals/overview.md` and a pointer at the end of the Components tab guide.

The guide content is grounded in the DevTools source in this repo (`devtools/projects/ng-devtools`, e.g. `signal-graph-pane`, `signals-visualizer`, `signal-details`, and the `ɵgetSignalGraph` debug API in `packages/core/src/render3/util/signal_debug.ts`); no screenshots yet — happy to add them if a maintainer can capture or point me at canonical ones.

Version support note: the signal graph requires an app built with Angular 19+ in development mode; DevTools shows the **Show Signal Graph** button automatically when the inspected app exposes the signal-graph debug API.

Issues.Title: fix(platform-browser): escape newlines in Meta selector values
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`escapeSelectorValue` escapes backslashes and double quotes to keep a value confined inside the `meta[name="..."]` selector that `parseSelector` derives. a newline cannot be confined that way: it terminates the string token ([CSS Syntax 3 4.3.5](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#consume-string-token)), and carriage return and form feed are preprocessed into one ([3.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#input-preprocessing)). so a `name` or `property` holding one of them produces a bad-string token, and the selector is invalid:

```ts
metaService.addTag({name: 'description\nevil', content: 'x'});
// DOMException: 'meta[name="description
// evil"]' is not a valid selector
```

the throw comes from `querySelector` inside `getTags`, so it escapes `addTag`, `updateTag`, `getTag` and `removeTag`. it is reachable wherever the tag name is taken from content rather than written literally, which is the normal shape for og/twitter tags driven by a cms or an api response.

found while auditing the css-escaping helpers in `common` and `platform-browser` against each other: `escapeCssUrl` in `ng_optimized_image` already handles these characters and cites the same rule, and `viewport_scroller` defers to `CSS.escape`. this was the one that did not.

## What is the new behavior?

newline, carriage return and form feed are written as css character escapes (`\a `, `\d `, `\c `), which represent the same code points inside the string, so the value round-trips and the tag is matched. values without those characters serialize byte for byte as before.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

regression test added in `meta_spec.ts`. it fails on `main` in both `test_web_chromium` and `test_web_firefox` with the `is not a valid selector` error above and passes with this change. note the `:test` target would not have caught it, since domino accepts the invalid selector where browsers reject it.

Issues.Title: docs: clarify streaming resource data flow
Issues.Body:
Clarify the Streaming Resources documentation to make the data flow between the source signal and the resource explicit.

- Explain that `stream` should return a signal representing a continuously updating data source.
- Clarify that the resource consumes the signal's value and updates when the signal changes.
- Explain that `userUpdates` simulates an external source such as WebSocket or SSE.
- Update the example comment to make the direction of the data flow explicit.
- Distinguish `stream` from `loader` for continuously updating versus one-time asynchronous operations.

## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The Streaming Resources documentation does not clearly explain the data flow between the source signal and the resource.

The current example may give the impression that the Resource updates the source signal, rather than consuming a signal that represents an external, continuously updating data source.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

The documentation now explicitly explains that:

- `stream` should return a signal representing a continuously updating data source.
- The resource consumes the signal's current value and updates when the signal changes.
- The example simulates values arriving from an external source such as a WebSocket or Server-Sent Events (SSE) connection.
- The distinction between stream and loader is clarified: stream is intended for continuously updating sources, while loader is intended for one-time asynchronous operations.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

This PR only updates the documentation and example comments. It does not modify the Resource API or application behavior.

Issues.Title: fix(core): do not swallow compilation errors in computeStandaloneComponentScope
Issues.Body:
Previously, `DepsTracker.computeStandaloneComponentScope` called `verifyStandaloneImport(imported, type)` inside a `try/catch` block to check whether an imported type was standalone or an `NgModule`.

In JIT mode with `ngDevMode=false` (where `directiveDefs()` skips its own `verifyStandaloneImport` pass), `computeStandaloneComponentScope` is the first place that reads the lazy definition getter (e.g. `ɵdir`) of an imported directive, which triggers JIT compilation of that directive. Any compilation error thrown while compiling the imported directive (such as an invalid host binding like `@HostBinding('attr.onclick')`) was caught by the `try/catch` block and silently swallowed by poisoning the scope instead of surfacing the compilation error.

This change replaces the `try { verifyStandaloneImport(...) } catch` check in `computeStandaloneComponentScope` with direct `isNgModule(imported)` and `isStandalone(imported)` checks (matching `computeNgModuleScope`), ensuring compilation errors thrown while evaluating imported definitions are not swallowed, and migrates the `security_integration_spec.ts` host binding test to standalone.

Both files list and refer to the tools as `devserver_start`, `devserver_stop` and `devserver_wait_for_build`. This is a text-only change (9 lines). Table alignment is unchanged because the new names are the same length.

Issues.Title: docs: correct how multiple route guards are executed
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The route guards guide and the `angular-developer` agent skill say that multiple guards in an array "are executed in the order they appear in the array".

That is not accurate for asynchronous guards. The router subscribes to every guard in the array (`prioritizedGuardValue` uses `combineLatest`), so guards that return a `Promise` or `Observable` run concurrently. Array order only decides which result takes priority.

Reproduction on `@angular/router` 22.2.1 with `canActivate: [authGuard, dataGuard]`, where `authGuard` resolves `false` after 100ms and `dataGuard` resolves `true` after 10ms:

    20ms  authGuard start
    20ms  dataGuard start
    32ms  dataGuard end -> true
    132ms authGuard end -> false   (navigation resolves false)

With `[g1 (slow, returns a UrlTree), g2 (fast, returns false)]`, the router waits for `g1` and redirects, so the first non-`true` result in array order wins.

A reader, or an AI agent following the skill, can therefore write a guard that assumes an earlier guard has already finished, for example by loading the current user.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

- `adev/.../route-guards.md` now says guards start in array order but do not wait for each other, that array order sets result priority, and adds a note not to depend on work done by an earlier guard in the same array.
- `skills/.../route-guards.md` gets the same correction.

No code or behavior changes. Making guards run sequentially is a separate design question (see #21702) and is not addressed here.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(core): widen the node injector index in RelativeInjectorLocation …
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`RelativeInjectorLocation` packs the index of the parent node injector into 15 bits (`InjectorIndexMask = 0b111111111111111`), and `getParentInjectorLocation()` stores `tNode.injectorIndex` without a range check. Every element with a directive costs ~11 `LView` slots (node, directive instance, 9 injector slots), so a template with roughly 2,900 such elements pushes injector indices past 32767. Descendants and child-component nodes then get a truncated parent index, which shows up as `ASSERTION ERROR: Parent injector must be pointing past HEADER_OFFSET` in dev mode, `RangeError: Invalid string length` / `Maximum call stack size exceeded` in production, or a bogus `NG0201: No provider found` when the corrupted cumulative bloom filter stops the lookup early.

Issue Number: #53245

## What is the new behavior?

The index occupies 20 bits and the view offset starts at bit 20 (`ViewOffsetShift = 20`). The value stays within V8's 31-bit small-integer range for up to 1023 nested declaration views (lexical template nesting). Templates with up to ~95,000 directive-bearing elements per `LView` now resolve their parent injectors correctly. Nothing changes for templates below the previous limit: encode and decode remain symmetric and the lookup is still one AND and one shift.

An acceptance test renders 3,000 child components whose inner directive injects a directive provided on an ancestor element and verifies every one resolves the same instance.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

The change was validated by applying the same constants to the published `@angular/core` 22.2.1 bundle and running the reproduction from #53245 (3,000 and 12,000 hosts, dev and prod mode, the `NG0201` variant and the >= 65536 variant), plus the cases with non-zero view offsets (`@for`, `*ngIf`, `@if` blocks, nested components). The acceptance test was not run under Bazel locally (Windows); CI will.

Issues.Title: fix(core): defer destroying an effect until its current run ends
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When an effect calls `destroy()` on itself and then reads a signal in the same run, it's added back as a consumer of that signal:

```ts
const ref = effect(() => {
  if (!ready()) return;
  ref.destroy();
  settings.theme(); // links the destroyed effect to `theme` again
});
```

`consumerDestroy()` removes the effect's links, but the effect is still the active consumer until the run ends, and effect nodes are always live. A long-lived signal then keeps the destroyed effect reachable, and for a view effect, the view of the destroyed component too.

Cleanup functions registered after `destroy()` in the same run are never called either, because `destroy()` has already run the cleanups.

Issue Number: Fixes #71220

## What is the new behavior?

When `destroy()` is called while the effect is running, it only marks the effect, and `run()` destroys it once the run ends. At that point the effect is no longer the active consumer, so its links stay dropped, and every cleanup registered during the run is called. This also covers an effect that is destroyed indirectly during its run, for example when it destroys its own component.

I added three tests: a root effect and a view effect that read a signal after destroying themselves, and a root effect that registers a cleanup after `destroy()`. All three fail without the change.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

A destroyed effect still never runs again. What changes is that the signals it read after `destroy()` no longer keep it, or its view, alive, and that cleanups registered after `destroy()` are now called.

One timing difference: cleanups registered earlier in the same run used to be called inside `destroy()`. They're now called right after the effect function returns.

`afterRender` sequences already work this way: `AfterRenderManager.unregister()` doesn't remove a sequence while hooks are executing, it marks it so it's removed once the execution ends.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): give duplicated and frozen array items their own field
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #70840

A signal form array field is looked up by the tracking symbol stored on each item. Nothing stops two entries from carrying the same symbol, so a `{...item}` copy resolves to the original item's field and writes land in the wrong row. Assigning the symbol also throws on frozen items.

## What is the new behavior?

- The first item keeps a claimed tracking key and a later copy gets a fresh one. A plain `{...item}` update of the same row keeps its field.
- The same object repeated in an array, and non-extensible (for example frozen) objects, are tracked by index, like primitives.
- An index-tracked element gets its own field instead of reusing one that belongs to another item, whether that item is elsewhere in the array or was removed from it.
- Writing through an index-tracked field drops the tracking key the written copy inherited, so the item stays on that field and keeps its touched and dirty state. This covers frozen data such as Apollo results, as noted on the issue.

Nine tests in `field_node.spec.ts` cover these cases; all nine fail without the change. `//packages/forms/signals/...` and `//packages/forms/test/...` pass.

When a copy is inserted before its original, the earlier index keeps the field. I asked on the issue whether that is acceptable; happy to change it.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: Security: distinct HTML attributes stall Angular SSR workers during sanitization
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core, platform-server (the pinned Domino HTML parser) ### Is this a regression? No. ### Description **Security impact: SSR availability.** When an application renders lower-trust HTML through a normal `[innerHTML]` binding during server-side rendering, one element with many *distinct* attributes can occupy a Node.js worker for seconds. The sanitizer eventually removes those attributes, but Domino parses them first. An attacker who can submit such content and request its page can delay otherwise valid requests served by the same worker. In a two-worker deployment, one stored article and one GET per worker delayed valid requests to both workers for about 20 seconds. The current Angular `main` lockfile pins Domino commit `1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727`. In that revision, [`handleSimpleAttribute()`](https://github.com/angular/domino/blob/1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727/lib/HTMLParser.js#L2336-L2365) scans every previously parsed attribute name before appending a new one. [`addAttribute()`](https://github.com/angular/domino/blob/1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727/lib/HTMLParser.js#L2320-L2333) does the same. A single element with distinct names therefore causes quadratic name-comparison work. Angular's [SSR HTML sanitizer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/439d495aaa53ebce35e46464a08b5fb10a5ecd61/packages/core/src/sanitization/html_sanitizer.ts#L304-L333) constructs and reparses an inert document before it can strip the attributes. Minimal input generator: ```js const html = ` ` a${i}="x"`).join('')}>x`; // 538,902 UTF-8 bytes; 50,000 distinct, nonnumeric attribute names. ``` To reproduce the lower-trust path, accept this as a submitted Markdown article with raw HTML enabled (for example, Marked 18.0.11), then render the parsed article in a generated Angular SSR page containing `
`. The tested app used `AngularNodeAppEngine` and `REQUEST_CONTEXT`; it did not use `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, a custom sanitizer, or a patched framework. The submission cap was 1 MiB. `POST /submit` stored the article; `GET /article` triggered SSR. The attacker can make that GET without waiting for another reader. On an exact-main production build, Node v24.21.0, macOS arm64, default heap and stack settings, and `optimization.styles.inlineCritical: false`: | 538,902-byte input | Article GET | Valid benign POST started 2 s later | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Same-size plain HTML text, one worker | 22 ms | 6 ms | | 50,000 duplicate attributes with size-matched filler, one worker | 38 ms | 2 ms | | 50,000 distinct attributes, fresh worker 1 | 11,405 ms | 9,403 ms | | 50,000 distinct attributes, fresh worker 2 | 12,714 ms | 10,710 ms | | Same-size plain HTML text, two workers | 23 / 72 ms | 4 / 4 ms | | 50,000 distinct attributes, two workers | 21,999 / 21,902 ms | 19,996 / 19,901 ms | All article requests returned 200, all benign POSTs returned 201, and the workers survived. The attack response contained sanitized `
x
`; the raw attributes did not survive. The benign POST handler does not parse the stored article, so its delay reflects worker unavailability rather than additional processing of the attack input. The HTTP reproduction used Angular main `7d96a37af4f7b7dd9dc9a2b9b90cc043c7da2a31` and CLI main `564d6d83151b993c4d6825f91fcac033470a35f6`. On 2026-10-06, Angular main had advanced to `439d495aaa53ebce35e46464a08b5fb10a5ecd61`; the Domino pin, sanitizer, inert-document helper, and Domino adapter remained unchanged. Released Angular 22.2.0 also showed the stall in a separate run. This requires an application workflow that accepts substantial raw HTML from a lower-trust actor and SSR renders it through `[innerHTML]`. Sites that reject raw HTML or cap attribute counts do not have the demonstrated path. The observed consequence is worker starvation, not a process crash or a demonstrated outage of every deployment. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug Standalone released-package reproduction: https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-ssr-attribute-parser-stall-repro It contains the SSR app, pinned npm lockfile, same-byte controls, and a validator. Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and `npm run validate` on supported Node 24.x. The input generator, path, and measured controls are also summarized above. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No exception. The worker remained alive but could not promptly serve another valid request while sanitizing the article. ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) Angular core and platform-server built from `7d96a37af4f7b7dd9dc9a2b9b90cc043c7da2a31`; Angular CLI/SSR built from `564d6d83151b993c4d6825f91fcac033470a35f6`; Domino pin `1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727`; Node v24.21.0; macOS 26.6.2 arm64. A released Angular 22.2.0 run provided secondary evidence. ### Anything else? This is distinct from #70826 (numeric attribute sparse storage), #70926 (active-formatting reconstruction), and #71195 (deep-tree owner recursion). The input here is a well-formed single `
` with distinct nonnumeric names. Avoiding repeated linear scans of preceding names, or otherwise bounding parser work per element, would address the observed cost.

Issues.Title: dev-server: es2016 prebundle target for zone.js apps lowers private fields and breaks dependencies
Issues.Body:
## Command

serve

## Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

## The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.0.1

## Description

Since #33772 (22.1.4), the dev server prebundles dependencies with an `es2016` target for zone.js apps, so async/await gets lowered (#33770). But rolldown can't lower only async/await like esbuild's `supported: { 'async-await': false }` did. With `es2016`, it lowers everything newer, including private fields.

That hits an oxc bug: when a static private field is lowered, the helper references the class by name, and if the method has a local with the same name, it reads the local in its TDZ. Minified libraries hit this easily, because the minifier reuses `t` for both. In our case iX modals can't be closed anymore in `ng serve`. Production is fine, since it doesn't prebundle and esbuild only lowers async/await.

The oxc bug itself: https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27376

I know the actual bug is in oxc, but every zone.js app now runs all its dependencies through a much bigger transform in dev than in production, which is how we ran into it. It'd be great if the prebundle could only lower async/await again. One idea: the prebundle already runs Angular's Babel step for the linker, so `@babel/plugin-transform-async-to-generator` could do it there and rolldown could keep the real browser targets. I didn't test that though.

## Minimal Reproduction

https://github.com/felix-eschey/ix-modal

```sh
git clone https://github.com/felix-eschey/ix-modal && cd ix-modal
npm ci
npm run broken    # ng serve on http://localhost:4300 with zone.js
```

Open http://localhost:4300, click "Open modal" and then Cancel. The modal stays open and the console shows the `ReferenceError`. `npm run working` is the same app without zone.js and works. `npm run excluded` keeps zone.js but excludes iX from `prebundle` and works too.

## Exception or Error

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access 't' before initialization
    at t$8.ensureCache (p-BqeSHO6C.js:1:304)
    at get mediumTime (p-BqeSHO6C.js:1:1189)
```

## Your Environment

```
Angular CLI       : 22.1.7
Angular           : 22.1.6
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : linux x64

@angular/build    : 22.1.7
zone.js           : 0.15.1
```

## Anything else relevant?

Workaround is `prebundle: { exclude: [...] }` for the affected packages. iX issue: https://github.com/siemens/ix/issues/2874

Issues.Title: @angular/cli 21.2.x and 20.3.x depend on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0 which is vulnerable to CVE-2026-104850
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h (CVE-2026-104850, CVSS 7.5): "MCP TypeScript SDK: OAuth client could send credentials to an authorization server chosen by the MCP server".

Affected range: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk >= 1.12.0, < 1.31.0` (so 1.30.1 is affected too), patched in `1.31.0`.

Both LTS branches pin a vulnerable version exactly (locked on, no update allowed):

- v21 LTS: `@angular/cli` 21.2.21 through 21.2.25 (latest) depend on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0` (earlier 21.2.x pinned 1.26.0, also affected)
- v20 LTS: `@angular/cli` 20.3.34 through 20.3.38 (latest) depend on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0` (earlier 20.3.x pinned 1.26.0, also affected)

v22 (22.2.x) is not affected, since it depends on `@modelcontextprotocol/server` instead.

The fix would be bumping `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to `1.31.0` (or later) on both branches, as was done for #33787 (#33789 / #33790).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. npm install @angular/cli@21 (or @angular/cli@20)
2. npm audit

### Exception or Error

```text
# npm audit report

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk  1.12.0 - 1.30.1
Severity: high
MCP TypeScript SDK: OAuth client could send credentials to an authorization server chosen by the MCP server - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h
fix available via `npm audit fix --force`
Will install @angular/cli@22.2.1, which is a breaking change
node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk
  @angular/cli  20.1.0-next.0 - 22.2.0-rc.0
  Depends on vulnerable versions of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
  node_modules/@angular/cli
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 21.2.25 / 20.3.38
Package Manager   : npm
```

### Anything else relevant?

_No response_

##### Minor Changes

- [#​2929](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2929) [`40f8f4e`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/40f8f4e229d963cd7fd2890bda2aeebe7005299a) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `requireBearerAuth` and `verifyBearerToken` take a new optional `expectedResource`, which makes them accept only tokens issued for this resource (the token's audience). Set it to the value your authorization server puts into tokens meant for this server, usually the server's URL. When it is set, a token is accepted only if the verifier reports that value in `AuthInfo.resource`; the two are compared as strings, ignoring a fragment and one trailing slash. A token reported for another value, or for none, is answered `401 invalid_token` with the usual `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. When it is not set, nothing changes. To use it, pass `expectedResource` and have `verifyAccessToken` fill `AuthInfo.resource`, for example from the `aud` claim. The option is declared on a new exported type, `VerifyBearerTokenOptions`, which extends `BearerAuthOptions`; `BearerAuthOptions` itself is unchanged. The Express `requireBearerAuth` passes the option through. With Express, `@modelcontextprotocol/express` has to be upgraded to this release as well: 2.0.1 does not pass the option on, so nothing is compared. Its options type does not have the option, so TypeScript reports an `expectedResource` written in a call to the 2.0.1 `requireBearerAuth` as an error.

- [#​2926](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2926) [`6d8dbc6`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/6d8dbc6cb590edf766fcb66b636ca6b654e99c37) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `McpServer` now accepts a `maxToolInputElements` option that limits the number of elements in tool-call arguments: the largest combined number of array elements and object members a single `tools/call` `arguments` payload may contain. It is off by default, so behavior is unchanged unless you set it. When it is set and a call exceeds it, that call is answered with an `isError: true` tool result that names the limit, before the input schema runs, and the server keeps serving. Set it above the largest arguments your tools legitimately accept; `maxRequestBodySize` remains the primary limit on request size. The value must be a number of at least 1, or `Infinity` for no limit; any other value is rejected at construction. The options type is exported as `McpServerOptions`.

- [#​2918](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2918) [`84804c2`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/84804c22e45a662675a198f853b7f00063838a8d) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A `Server` or `McpServer` now serves one connection at a time, and a Streamable HTTP server transport without sessions (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`) serves one request. An app that uses one server object, or one stateless transport, for every HTTP request fails on the second request after this upgrade. Build the server and the transport per request instead.

  What keeps working without a change:

  - `createMcpHandler(buildServer)` and `serveStdio(buildServer)`, where `buildServer` returns a new server on every call.
  - A handler that builds a new server and a new stateless transport for each request.
  - One server and one transport per session (a transport with a `sessionIdGenerator`).
  - Connecting a server again after `close()`.
  - `Client`.

  What fails now, how it shows, and what to change:

  - One server object with a new stateless transport per request (`const server = new McpServer(...)` outside the handler, `await server.connect(transport)` inside it): the second HTTP request the process receives fails, and so does every later one. `connect()` rejects with an `SdkError` of code `ALREADY_CONNECTED`. If the handler closes the transport when the response ends, requests that arrive one after the other still work and a request that overlaps another one fails. Change: move `new McpServer(...)` and its registrations into the handler.
  - One stateless transport for every request (a transport built once with `sessionIdGenerator: undefined`): the second HTTP request fails. `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest()` rejects with `Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests. Create a new transport per request.`, and `NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest()` answers `500`. Change: build the server and the transport inside the handler and connect them there.
  - `createMcpHandler(() => server)` with a server built once: a request that arrives after the previous response has been read to its end still works. A request that arrives while another one is being served is answered `500` with the JSON-RPC error `-32603` (`Internal server error`); the reason is reported only through the `onerror` option. Change: pass a function that builds the server, as in `createMcpHandler(buildServer)`.
  - One server object for every session: the `initialize` request of the second session fails with `ALREADY_CONNECTED`. Change: build a server per session.

  What the caller sees when `connect()` or `handleRequest()` rejects depends on the host. Express 5, Fastify and Hono answer `500`. A plain `node:http` listener without its own error handling gets an unhandled rejection, which ends the process.

  The README examples of `@modelcontextprotocol/express`, `@modelcontextprotocol/fastify`, `@modelcontextprotocol/hono` and `@modelcontextprotocol/node`, and the handler examples in the JSDoc of `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` and `NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport`, now build a server and a transport per request.

- [#​2907](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2907) [`e55f9ac`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/e55f9ac1b1cae413599b499cbaa45c0378edba78) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `allowedOrigins` and `validateOriginHeader` accept lowercase entries of the form `<scheme>://*`, such as `moz-extension://*` or `chrome-extension://*`, which admit every origin of that scheme. This lets a server admit MCP clients that run as a browser extension when the extension ID cannot be listed, as on Firefox, where it differs on every install. `http://*` and `https://*` are not honoured, and the defaults are unchanged.

### [`v2.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol/server%402.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/compare/@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0...@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.1.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​1624](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/1624) [`6032170`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/60321700871029401a2e3bed8fdf4f02c9ec3331) Thanks [@​SamMorrowDrums](https://redirect.github.com/SamMorrowDrums)! - Add request-time OAuth scope challenges for tools, resources, resource templates,
  and prompts. Each primitive's `scopeChallenge` callback receives the parsed
  request and verified authentication info, then either continues or returns the
  exact scope set for an `insufficient_scope` response. `requireScopes` provides a
  small helper for static all-of checks.

  `createMcpHandler` and Streamable HTTP transports return HTTP 403 with an
  `insufficient_scope` challenge before handler execution or SSE setup. The
  preflight is active whenever a registered primitive carries a `scopeChallenge`
  callback — there is no handler- or transport-level configuration. The
  challenge's `WWW-Authenticate` header is built by the same formatter as the
  bearer-auth 401/403 answers, and its `resource_metadata` parameter is derived
  from the verified `AuthInfo`: `requireBearerAuth` / `verifyBearerToken` now
  stamp their configured `resourceMetadataUrl` onto the `AuthInfo` they return
  (new optional `AuthInfo.resourceMetadataUrl` field), with a fallback to the
  well-known location for an HTTP(S) RFC 8707 `resource` identifier; the
  parameter is omitted when neither is available.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​2726](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2726) [`6fa4227`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/6fa42279fecaba423635072f716bbb2f6f7c77f3) Thanks [@​LuckTerence](https://redirect.github.com/LuckTerence)! - `SdkError` and `SdkHttpError` accept standard `ErrorOptions` as an optional fourth constructor argument and forward it to `Error`, so a wrapped error is reachable through the standard `Error.cause` chain. Version-negotiation probe failures (`SdkErrorCode.EraNegotiationFailed`) now use it: the underlying `TypeError: fetch failed` and the DNS or socket error beneath it surface via `error.cause`, so pino, Sentry, and `util.inspect` render `ENOTFOUND` / `ECONNREFUSED` / `ETIMEDOUT` instead of stopping at the `SdkError` ([#​2657](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/issues/2657)). The previous `error.data.cause` slot is still populated for compatibility but is deprecated and slated for removal; read `error.cause` instead.

- [#​2654](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2654) [`03842cd`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/03842cd9cae9a9b142c77d2fb65e829fc4e03eab) Thanks [@​pshah19](https://redirect.github.com/pshah19)! - Treat request id `0` as a real id. Two guards tested a `RequestId` for truthiness, so the legal JSON-RPC ids `0` and `''` were read as absent. Id `0` is not a corner case: the outbound request counter is zero-based, so it is the first id every peer assigns, which on the server→client leg is the first `sampling/createMessage`, `elicitation/create`, or `roots/list` a server sends.

  - `notifications/cancelled` carrying id `0` was ignored, and the in-flight handler ran to completion with its `AbortSignal` never fired.
  - A notification sent with `relatedRequestId: 0` wrongly passed the debounce gate (for methods opted into `debouncedNotificationMethods`). Because the pending set is keyed by method alone, a second such notification in the same tick was silently dropped rather than sent.

  Absent is now the only value that means "no id".

- [#​2668](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2668) [`3e90449`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/3e90449fd52997da43b79a536d2c19c446603cc7) Thanks [@​KKonstantinov](https://redirect.github.com/KKonstantinov)! - Stop sending `notifications/cancelled` for the `initialize` handshake. The spec is explicit that a client MUST NOT attempt to cancel its `initialize` request, but the outbound cancel path fired for any in-flight request: aborting the `AbortSignal` passed to `connect()`, or letting the handshake hit its timeout, put a forbidden cancellation on the wire naming the initialize request id.

  The local behaviour is unchanged — the caller's promise still rejects with the same abort/timeout error, and `connect()` still tears the connection down. Only the wire notification is suppressed. Every other method keeps the existing cancellation path.

- [#​2698](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2698) [`7b781ed`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/7b781ed4e25355a25d15974f3c76de81299694ed) Thanks [@​maxisbey](https://redirect.github.com/maxisbey)! - Read Streamable HTTP request bodies with a size limit. Every SDK-owned body read —
  `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` (and the Node transport built on it),
  `createMcpHandler`, `toNodeHandler`, and `createMcpHonoApp`'s JSON pre-parse — now stops at
  4 MiB by default (the limit the legacy SSE transport already uses; the Express adapter and stdio
  bound their reads too) and answers `413 Payload Too Large` before anything is parsed.
  `toWebRequest` (when it reads the Node stream itself) now rejects once the body exceeds the
  limit with an error whose `name` is `'RequestBodyTooLargeError'` and `status` is `413`, and
  `toNodeHandler` answers that with `413`; hand-wired callers of `toWebRequest` should handle the
  rejection or pass a pre-parsed body, and `isLegacyRequest` reports such a request as non-legacy
  so the modern handler answers it. JSON-RPC batch arrays are limited to 100 messages; a longer
  batch is answered `400` / `-32600` and none of it is dispatched.

  The limit is configurable with a new `maxRequestBodySize` option (bytes, default
  `DEFAULT_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` = 4 MiB, exported from `@modelcontextprotocol/server`) on
  `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransportOptions`, `CreateMcpHandlerOptions` (forwarded to its
  stateless legacy leg; `isLegacyRequest` and `legacyStatelessFallback` take the same option),
  `CreateMcpHonoAppOptions`, and `ToNodeHandlerOptions` / `ToWebRequestOptions` (the adapter's
  bound applies before the handler's, so raise both). The bounded reader is exported as
  `readRequestBody` for adapter authors. Hosts that pre-parse the body and pass it as
  `parsedBody` skip the SDK's read and its size limit entirely; the batch bound applies either way.

  `createMcpHonoApp` and `createMcpExpressApp` now run their Host/Origin validation before the
  JSON body parser, so a request from a disallowed Host or Origin with an invalid JSON body is
  answered `403` rather than `400`, and its body is not read.

- [#​2590](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2590) [`75dc7ea`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/75dc7ea6e2913e1ac37d4f06eec62cd5cfac9e7a) Thanks [@​davidpavlovschi](https://redirect.github.com/davidpavlovschi)! - Reject a modern (2026-07-28) POST that omits the required `MCP-Protocol-Version` header.

  `createMcpHandler` accepted a request whose body carried a valid per-request `_meta`
  envelope but whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header was absent: the request was classified
  modern, dispatched, and answered `200` — tool handlers ran. Only the *mismatch* case
  (header present, disagreeing with the body) was rejected, so of the standard headers
  SEP-2243 requires on a modern POST, presence was enforced for `Mcp-Method` (and for
  `Mcp-Name` on the methods that mirror `params.name` / `params.uri`) but not for
  `MCP-Protocol-Version`.

  Such a request is now refused with `400 Bad Request` and JSON-RPC `-32020`
  (`HeaderMismatch`), matching the shape the sibling missing-header cells already emit and
  echoing the request id — per the Streamable HTTP spec, which requires the header on every
  POST and lists a missing required standard header as a `HeaderMismatch` failure. The
  spec's allowance to treat a header-less request as `2025-03-26` is available only to a
  server that also serves pre-2025-06-18 clients, and permits routing it to *legacy*
  handling — never serving it as 2026-07-28; under `legacy: 'reject'` the requirement is
  unconditional.

  Era classification is deliberately unchanged and stays body-primary: a proxy that strips
  the header still must not change the era, so such a request is still *classified* modern
  and is refused one rung later, at `standard-header-validation` — the same rung that
  already answers a missing `Mcp-Method`. Legacy-era traffic is untouched, notifications
  are unaffected, body-less `GET` / `DELETE` session operations are method-routed before
  any header validation, and stdio serving (which has no HTTP headers) is not involved.

  Clients built with this SDK always send the header, so no first-party client is affected;
  hand-rolled clients that omitted it must add it.

- [#​2494](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2494) [`6a05402`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/6a054025e8cebaecead76fb51d92ba3974e8d091) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `StdioServerTransport` now closes itself and fires `onclose` when its stdin ends or closes. The stdio binding says servers "SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed" — stdin EOF is the primary graceful-shutdown signal, and on some platforms (notably Windows, where no signal is delivered when the parent goes away) the only reliable one. Previously the transport listened only for `data` and `error`, so when an MCP client hung up its end of the pipe (window closed, session restarted, host crashed) the server never noticed: `onclose` never fired, nothing tore down, and server processes accumulated as zombies until killed by hand. The transport now attaches `end`/`close` listeners on stdin that close the transport (idempotently — `onclose` still fires exactly once if `close()` is also called), so `Server`/`McpServer` and `serveStdio` tear down through the existing `onclose` chain and a well-behaved server process exits naturally. Requests still in flight when stdin ends are aborted (their handlers observe `signal.aborted`) and their responses are not written: EOF means the client has hung up and is no longer waiting. A client that wants answers keeps stdin open until it has read them.

- [#​2613](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2613) [`70de0c8`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/70de0c8b569b0d664a56b90be2f141d1d1645880) Thanks [@​jwcarman](https://redirect.github.com/jwcarman)! - Emit and validate the `Mcp-Name` header for tasks requests per SEP-2663's Streamable HTTP binding: the client transport now mirrors `params.taskId` into `Mcp-Name` on `tasks/get` / `tasks/update` / `tasks/cancel` (previously omitted, causing conforming servers to reject every task poll with `-32020 HeaderMismatch`), and the server-side standard-header validation cross-checks it via the same shared `MCP_NAME_HEADER_SOURCE` table.

  On the server, `createMcpHandler` now answers a modern (2026-07-28) `tasks/get` / `tasks/update` / `tasks/cancel` POST that omits `Mcp-Name`, or whose header disagrees with `params.taskId`, with `400` / `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) at the `standard-header-validation` rung, the same treatment `tools/call` / `prompts/get` / `resources/read` already get. Legacy-era (2025-11-25) tasks traffic is unaffected. Clients built with this SDK release send the header; hand-rolled clients that omitted it must add it.

- Updated dependencies \[[`dcc0102`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/dcc01028ff6a499a5728c2b6181c1727d52e2fab)]:
  - [@​modelcontextprotocol/core](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/core)@2.1.0

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): generate main.ts with lint-compatible error handling
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

Documentation changes are not needed for this generated-code correction.

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Applications generated by `ng new` or `ng generate application` use an untyped catch callback and implicitly return `console.error(err)` in `main.ts`. With typed linting, this triggers `@typescript-eslint/use-unknown-in-catch-callback-variable` and `@typescript-eslint/no-confusing-void-expression`.

Closes #34267.

## What is the new behavior?

Both standalone and NgModule application templates declare the rejection parameter as `unknown` and log the error inside a block body:

```ts
.catch((err: unknown) => {
  console.error(err);
});
```

Application schematic tests cover both variants and verify the explicit parameter type and block body. Bootstrap and error logging behavior are preserved. Existing applications do not require a migration.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Validation:

- `pnpm bazel test //packages/schematics/angular:test` — passed.
- ESLint and Prettier checks for `application/index_spec.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

The full `pnpm bazel test //packages/...` attempt was interrupted and reported 78 passing targets, 3 local failures, and 18 skipped targets. The failures are outside the changed files:

- `//packages/angular_devkit/core/node:test`: `NodeJsAsyncHost can watch` expected 3 events but received 4.
- `//packages/angular_devkit/build_webpack:build_webpack_test`: timeout.
- `//packages/ngtools/webpack:test`: timeout.

The full suite did not pass. No end-to-end suite was run.

Issues.Title: Follow-up to issue: SSR: Add a way to configure externalDependencies for the server bundle only
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Description

As title says, I'd like to follow-up on the unfortunately closed issue https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/26487, requesting to configure externalDependencies independently for server and browser bundle.

Reading the mentioned issue, it has been closed because no particular value has been seen in being able to configure externalDependencies independently. However I'd like to point to a realistic and important case where such an option will be crucial. 

Right now, we're still on using Webpack, which allows configuring externalDependencies explicitly for the server bundle, and that's the reason why it's not blocking us yet. But there's plans to eventually migrate to application-builder, however still a lot of obstacles ned to be solved, as like the mentioned lack of being able to define externalDependencies for server bundle only.

Our case is, we're using DataDog `dd-trace` for monitoring our server app infrastructure. dd-trace is being injected on runtime and requires all node packages doing downstream requests being external as otherwise it cannot properly trace them. See https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/trace_collection/dd_libraries/nodejs/#bundling

In our particular scenario, this applies to `graphql` package. We had to externalize it, as otherwise we wouldn't get logs for all requests towards our GraphQL API on server-side. But on the client-side using the browser-bundle we do not want `graphql` package being external, as there's absolutely no reason in it.

So, our particular needs can be properly served by using Webpack builder but with the current options for application-builder this isn't possible.

As a workaround I tried to implement a custom Esbuild plugin, which should reset the external dependencies just for the browser build. But due to the Angular build architecture this only works for a prod build but not for a development build. So I eventually dropped this idea, which anyway doesn't seem clean.

Hence I'd highly appreciate if you could change your mind in considering separate externalDependencies configurations for server and browser build.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Being able to configure externalDependencies separately for server and browser build.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): keep proxy entry order and support a string `context`
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #34257

`normalizeProxyConfiguration` loses two things when it turns the proxy file into the object Vite expects:

- Glob keys are converted by adding the regex key and deleting the original one, so every glob entry ends up after the plain and `^` keys. With `{"/api/auth/**": ..., "/api/": ...}`, `/api/auth/login` goes to the `/api/` target.
- In the array form, an entry whose `context` is a single string (`context: '/api'`) is skipped, so nothing is proxied for it. The Webpack-based dev server accepts it.

## What is the new behavior?

- The normalized object is rebuilt in the original order, with glob keys converted in place.
- A string `context` is handled like a one-element array.

Each fix is in its own commit with a test in `proxy-config_spec.ts`. I checked that both tests fail without the fixes: the order test gets `OTHER_API_RETURN`, and the string `context` test gets `index.html`.

The third point of #34257 (globs and query strings) isn't part of this PR. For a trailing `/**`, picomatch puts a `$` inside the generated regex, so it takes more than appending an optional query string, and it changes which requests get proxied.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

A config that relied on globs being tried last, such as a catch-all `/**` written before more specific plain keys, will now match in the order it's written. That's also how the Webpack-based dev server handles it.

Issues.Title: Vite dev server: proxy config normalization reorders glob keys, drops string `context` and misses URLs with a query string
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

The webpack-based `@angular-devkit/build-angular:dev-server`

### Description

`normalizeProxyConfiguration` in `packages/angular/build/src/utils/load-proxy-config.ts` turns the proxy file into the object Vite expects. Three things get lost along the way. In each case the request isn't proxied and falls through to the app (`index.html`), and nothing shows up in the `ng serve` output.

1. **Glob entries lose their position.** Each glob key is replaced with `normalizedProxy[pattern] = …; delete normalizedProxy[key]`, which moves it to the end of the object. Vite uses the first entry that matches, so a specific glob written first loses to a broader plain key written after it.
2. **A string `context` drops the whole entry.** In the array form, an entry whose `context` isn't an array is skipped. webpack-dev-server passes `context` to http-proxy-middleware as `pathFilter`, which accepts a single string, so `context: '/legacy'` works there. The array form conversion was added after #25337 so that webpack-style configs keep working, and this case slipped through.
3. **Globs are matched against the URL including its query string.** The regex built by picomatch ends with `$` and Vite tests it against `req.url`, so `/search/**` matches `/search` but not `/search?q=angular`. http-proxy-middleware matches both globs and plain keys against the pathname only.

### Minimal Reproduction

A new app served by `@angular/build:dev-server`, plus a backend that echoes the port and URL it receives:

```js
// backend.mjs
import http from 'node:http';
for (const port of [3998, 3999]) {
  http.createServer((req, res) => res.end(`${port} got ${req.url}\n`)).listen(port);
}
```

**1. Order** with `ng serve --proxy-config proxy.conf.json`:

```json
{
  "/api/auth/**": {"target": "http://localhost:3998"},
  "/api/": {"target": "http://localhost:3999"}
}
```

`curl localhost:4200/api/auth/login` returns `3999 got /api/auth/login`. I expected it to go to 3998.

**2. String `context`** with `ng serve --proxy-config proxy.conf.mjs`:

```js
export default [{context: '/legacy', target: 'http://localhost:3999'}];
```

`curl localhost:4200/legacy/users` returns `index.html`. `loadProxyConfiguration` returns `{}` for this file.

**3. Query string** with `ng serve --proxy-config proxy.conf.json`:

```json
{
  "/search/**": {"target": "http://localhost:3999"}
}
```

`curl localhost:4200/search` is proxied, but `curl 'localhost:4200/search?q=angular'` returns `index.html`.

### Exception or Error

```text
None. The requests are just not proxied.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.0
Angular           : 22.2.0
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

@angular/build    : 22.2.0
@angular/cli      : 22.2.0
vite              : 8.3.0
```

The code is the same on `main`.

### Anything else relevant?

#34258 fixes the first two points. The third one isn't part of it: for a trailing `/**`, picomatch puts a `$` inside the generated regex, so it takes more than appending an optional query string, and it changes which requests get proxied.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): add CSP nonce to stylesheet and modulepreload link elements
Issues.Body:
Under strict Content Security Policies that do not include 'self' in `style-src` or `style-src-elem`, external stylesheets must be authorized via a cryptographic nonce.

This PR updates `addNonce` to also apply the CSP nonce to `<link>` elements whose `rel` contains `stylesheet` or `modulepreload`.

Closes #34255
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): add CSP nonce to stylesheet and modulepreload link elements" (#34256)

Issues.Title: Add CSP nonce to <link rel="stylesheet"> tags when ngCspNonce is set
Issues.Body:
### Command

build, serve

### Description

When `ngCspNonce` is set in `index.html`, the build copies the nonce onto inline `<style>` tags and onto `<script>` tags, including `<script src>` since #27875. It does not copy it onto the `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags generated for the global `styles` bundle.

So a strict, nonce-based CSP still has to allow `'self'` (or a host source) in `style-src` / `style-src-elem`. Otherwise the browser blocks the global stylesheet:

> Content-Security-Policy: The page's settings blocked a style (style-src-elem) at https://example.com/styles-RBGG4ONZ.css

This makes a nonce-only `style-src` impossible, even though everything else the build emits is already nonced: the critical inline `<style>`, the `ngCspMedia` loader `<script>`, `main-*.js`, and component styles added at runtime.

The responsible code is `addNonce`, which only handles `style` and `script`:
https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/23e3d44a7f051cd3bb67700b8d8407f73b7aa7f3/packages/angular/build/src/utils/index-file/nonce.ts#L21-L41

The stylesheet links are generated here, without a nonce:
https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/23e3d44a7f051cd3bb67700b8d8407f73b7aa7f3/packages/angular/build/src/utils/index-file/augment-index-html.ts#L186

**Reproduction** (`@angular/build` 22.1.0, `@angular/build:application`, production config with default `inlineCritical`):

1. `index.html`: `<app-root ngCspNonce="RANDOM_NONCE"></app-root>`
2. `ng build`
3. Output `index.html`:
   ```html
   <style nonce="RANDOM_NONCE">/* critical css */</style>
   <script nonce="RANDOM_NONCE">/* ngCspMedia loader */</script>
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles-XXXX.css" media="print" ngcspmedia="all">
   <noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="styles-XXXX.css"></noscript>
   ...
   <script src="main-XXXX.js" type="module" nonce="RANDOM_NONCE"></script>
   ```
4. Serve with `Content-Security-Policy: style-src 'nonce-RANDOM_NONCE'; script-src 'nonce-RANDOM_NONCE'`. The global stylesheet is blocked.

The `nonce` attribute is valid on `<link rel="stylesheet">`. The element's nonce is passed as the request's cryptographic nonce metadata and is checked against `style-src-elem`, and all current browsers support this. A hash source can't be used instead, because hashes don't match external stylesheets.

**Why not just allow `'self'`?**

`'self'` is an allowlist covering the whole origin. A nonce only authorizes the elements the server put into this particular response. That gap matters for styles too:

- **`'self'` covers the whole origin, not the app.** An Angular app is often served under a sub-path (`<base href>`, `--base-href`, `APP_BASE_HREF`) behind a reverse proxy, sharing its origin with other apps, an API, or file downloads. With `'self'`, any `text/css` response anywhere on that origin counts as a trusted stylesheet. That includes legacy apps, user-uploaded files and endpoints that echo input. The page's security then depends on everything else deployed on the origin.
- **Injected markup can load stylesheets.** Angular sanitizes bindings, but HTML can still get in through `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, server-side rendering of untrusted data, or third-party widgets. When scripts are blocked, injected CSS is the next tool for an attacker. With `'self'`, injected markup can load any same-origin stylesheet. With a nonce-only policy, it can load none, because it can't know the per-response nonce.
- **What CSS injection can do.** It can change the UI: hide or overlay elements, fake dialogs, phishing prompts, clickjacking-style redressing inside the page. Attribute-selector and `:has()` tricks can probe the DOM for things like CSRF tokens or input values. Strict `img-src`/`font-src` limit exfiltration, but they don't stop the UI attacks.
- **Allowlists are the weak part of CSP.** Research on real-world policies found that allowlist sources (including `'self'`) are routinely bypassable. The recommendation is nonce- or hash-based "strict CSP". See Weichselbaum et al., "CSP Is Dead, Long Live CSP!" (ACM CCS 2016), https://research.google/pubs/csp-is-dead-long-live-csp-on-the-insecurity-of-whitelists-and-the-future-of-content-security-policy/, and https://web.dev/articles/strict-csp. That work focuses on scripts, but the reasoning carries over to styles.

`style-src 'self'` is clearly less dangerous than `script-src 'self'`. This is a defense-in-depth request, and given everything else is already nonced it is a small, consistent change.

### Describe the solution you'd like

In `addNonce`, also add the nonce to `<link>` tags whose `rel` contains `stylesheet`, including the `<noscript>` fallback and the `media="print"` / `ngCspMedia` link created by critical CSS inlining. A minimal change:

```ts
rewriter.on('startTag', (tag) => {
  const isStylesheetLink =
    tag.tagName === 'link' &&
    tag.attrs.some((attr) => attr.name === 'rel' && attr.value.split(/\s+/).includes('stylesheet'));

  if (
    (tag.tagName === 'style' || tag.tagName === 'script' || isStylesheetLink) &&
    !tag.attrs.some((attr) => attr.name === 'nonce')
  ) {
    tag.attrs.push({ name: 'nonce', value: nonce });
  }

  rewriter.emitStartTag(tag);
});
```

It may also make sense to nonce `<link rel="modulepreload">` (and `rel="preload" as="script|style"`), because those requests are also checked against `script-src` / `style-src`.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

1. **Keep `'self'` in `style-src`.** This works, but it trusts every same-origin stylesheet rather than only the ones the server emitted (see "Why not just allow `'self'`?" above). It is the only reason `'self'` is still needed.
2. **`autoCsp`.** It generates hashes for inline scripts in a `<meta>` tag. It does not cover external stylesheets and does not work with a CSP sent as a response header.
3. **Hash sources.** Hashes don't match external stylesheets.
4. **Inline all global styles** (e.g. move them into a `ViewEncapsulation.None` root component so they are added at runtime with the nonce). This loses the separately cached stylesheet and runs into the component style budgets.
5. **Post-process `index.html` after `ng build`** (our current workaround). We use a build step that rewrites every `<link rel="stylesheet"` to `<link rel="stylesheet" nonce="…"` and fails the build if a link without a nonce is left over. It works, but every project with a strict CSP has to rebuild and maintain it. The application builder has no index-HTML transform hook where this could live.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Add CSP nonce to <link rel="stylesheet"> tags when ngCspNonce is set" (#34255)

Issues.Title: bug(material/sort): hover hint arrow on an unsorted header shows the active sort direction, not the resulting direction after click.
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

18

### Description

The hint arrow on an unsorted header uses the table's current direction, but a click sorts that header in its start direction (`matSortStart`, `asc` by default).

Last worked as expected on v18. Which can be seen on the docs page.

https://material.angular.dev/components/sort/overview (bugged)

https://v18.material.angular.dev/components/sort/overview (working)

### Reproduction

This can be reproduced on the docs page.

https://material.angular.dev/components/sort/overview

1. Sort the Calories column desc.
2. Hover the Fat column.
3. Note the direction of the hover hint arrow.
4. Click the Fat column to sort.
5. NOT sorted how the hint from three (3) suggested it would be.

### Expected Behavior

At step three in the reproduction description, the hover hint arrow should be pointed up.

### Actual Behavior

At step three in the reproduction description, the hover hint arrow is pointed down.

### Environment

- Angular: latest
- CDK/Material: latest
- Browser(s): all 
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): all
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(material/sort): hover hint arrow on an unsorted header shows the active sort direction, not the resulting direction after click." (#33933)

Issues.Title: bug(cdk/a11y): HighContrastModeDetector crashes with NG0205 when combined with withAutoCleanupInjectors()
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

### Root cause
`HighContrastModeDetector` is declared without `providedIn: 'root'`:

<link to _a11y-module-chunk.mjs HighContrastModeDetector class>

The first `inject(HighContrastModeDetector)` call from `A11yModule.constructor()` therefore creates the instance in the route-scoped injector that A11yModule is imported into (via a Material component). `withAutoCleanupInjectors()` tears down that injector on navigation. Next navigation triggers a fresh A11yModule constructor whose inject-chain references the destroyed injector → NG0205.

Fix suggestion: Add `providedIn: 'root'` to the `@Injectable` of HighContrastModeDetector (and audit the other a11y services for the same shape).

### Workaround
Add `HighContrastModeDetector` to root providers manually:
```ts
providers: [..., HighContrastModeDetector]





### Reproduction

- Angular 22.2.0, @angular/cdk 22.2.1
- `provideRouter(..., withAutoCleanupInjectors())`
- Lazy-loaded route uses any Angular Material component (MatInput, MatButton, MatDialog, ...)
- Navigate: /route-a → /route-b → /route-a  (triggers A11yModule twice)


### Expected Behavior

Navigation succeeds.




### Actual Behavior

Second visit to a route that imports A11yModule throws:
`ERROR Error: NG0205` (InjectorAlreadyDestroyed)

Stack bottoms out at `HighContrastModeDetector` factory being called in an already-destroyed route injector.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.0 (@angular/core, @angular/common, @angular/router, @angular/platform-browser, @angular/compiler-cli)
- @angular/cdk: 22.2.0 (also reproduced on 22.2.1 and 22.3.0-next.0 — unchanged a11y code)
- @angular/material: 22.2.0
- @angular/cli / @angular/build: 22.2.0
- Node: v24.15.0
- npm: 11.12.1
- TypeScript target: ES2022, moduleResolution: bundler, strict: true, strictTemplates: true
- Rendering: ZoneJS active (zoneless-compatible code via Signals)
- Browser (via Playwright): Chromium 153 (headless + headed)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (CI reproduces more frequently on Linux containers)
- Router config:
  provideRouter(
    routes,
    withComponentInputBinding(),
    withRouterConfig({ paramsInheritanceStrategy: "always" }),
    withPreloading(PreloadAllModules),
    withAutoCleanupInjectors(),
  )
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "bug(cdk/a11y): HighContrastModeDetector crashes with NG0205 when combined with withAutoCleanupInjectors()" (#33919)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/drag-drop): use consistent touch coordinates for bounded dragging
Issues.Body:
Use the event target's touch for page coordinates, matching the pickup offset. This keeps bounded dragging inside its container when another finger was already touching a different element.

Fixes #33026.

Validation: the regression fails in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit before the change (-290px instead of the bounded 100px). All 103 standalone drag specs pass in each engine using the current-source Jasmine/JIT harness. Five Chromium browser touch-input scenarios, including both touch orders and zoom followed by dragging, pass. TypeScript, TSLint and formatting pass.

The standard Bazel target stops before tests in `rules_angular` with TS5055 (generated declarations would overwrite input files). Physical touchscreen verification has not been performed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(cdk/drag-drop): use consistent touch coordinates for bounded dragging" (#33928)

Issues.Title: fix(material/table): allow flex footer rows to grow with their cells
Issues.Body:
Correct the flex footer-row selector so tall cells can expand their row, matching the header and body. Adds layout regressions for both native and flex tables.

Fixes #33709. Follows the selector correction proposed in #33710, which was closed without merging.

Validation: the flex regression fails before the fix (52px row around a 100px cell). All 38 table and data-source specs pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit using a local Jasmine/JIT harness against the current sources and compiled Sass. Type checking, TSLint, Stylelint, and formatting pass. The standard Bazel target is blocked before tests by Angular worker build errors; no CI configuration changes are included.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/testing): propagate task state to child environments
Issues.Body:
When creating a harness via `harnessForFixture`, we await `environment.forceStabilize()` before creating the component harness and its child environment. In newer versions of Safari, resuming from native `await` can escape the test zone back to the root zone. This caused child environments created afterwards to fail the `isInProxyZone()` check and omit `_taskState`, preventing `waitForTasksOutsideAngular` from tracking async tasks scheduled outside Angular.

These changes resolve the issue by propagating the task state from the parent `TestbedHarnessEnvironment` down to child environments created via `createEnvironment`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(cdk/testing): propagate task state to child environments" (#33924)

Issues.Title: fix(material/dialog): use a theme token for the backdrop color
Issues.Body:
Closes #33578

Give Material dialogs a default backdrop class that reads the dialog `scrim-color` token. The M3 default derives from the system scrim color at 32% opacity; M2 retains its existing black backdrop at 32% opacity. Custom backdrop classes keep their current behavior, and CDK styling is unchanged.

This follows the Material-specific `backdropClass` approach discussed in the issue. Added regression coverage for the system scrim color, token overrides, and custom class arrays.

Validated the Dialog suite in Chromium and Firefox, the CDK Dialog Chromium suite, Sass theme compilation, formatting, and lint for the changed TypeScript and Sass files. The new default/token assertions fail before the fix. Internal screenshot baselines are left for maintainers to review.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/dialog): use a theme token for the backdrop color" (#33923)
